states.active: Grow flowers in the meadow behind Edda's cottage.
states.bloomed: Edda has come out to the bench. Go and sit with her.
states.complete: Come back in a few weeks. Not years. Weeks.

journal.active: Edda Brenn's husband Jonas kept a garden behind their cottage. It gave up two springs after he did. I offered a spell.
journal.bloomed: The meadow is flowering. Edda came outside on her own. I should go to her.
journal.complete: Done, and noted, so that I remember: weeks, not years.

states.active: Plant flowers at Jonas's stone, under the oak past the bench.
states.planted: The flowers are in. Tell Edda.
states.book: Edda gave you her mother's book. Open your satchel (I) and study it.

journal.active: Pippa says Jonas's stone, up by the oak, has been left to the moss. Edda hasn't been able to go. I can at least do the thing I'm good at.
journal.planted: Blue by the kerb. I should tell Edda before she works it out from the bench.
journal.book: Edda gave me her mother's household book. There's a rhyme for stains in it that she insists is only a rhyme. I'm going to read it properly.
journal.complete: It was a spell. Edda's mother had real magic and used it on gravy for forty years. It took me an afternoon to learn what she never knew she had.

states.active: Clean the mossy statue by the road with Fläckfri.
states.found: Tell Pippa who the statue is.
states.complete: Say good morning to people, even when you don't know who they are.

journal.active: Pippa has said good morning to a mossed-over statue by the road every day, in case it's someone. I have a rhyme for moss now.
journal.found: The statue is me. I should tell Pippa before she tells the statue.
journal.complete: A statue by the road, and a girl who said good morning to it for a year. The village remembered me better than I remember the village.
